native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB:
HYPOTHESIS (natural language, submission-ready):

"Diversity in Pottery Form collapsed while Diversity in Pottery Decoration simultaneously increased in the 18th century BCE (conventional century naming, 1800–1701 BCE; note that under the alternative labeling convention this same period is sometimes called the 17th century BCE). In the data, the change occurs between the 1800 BCE and 1700 BCE 100-year bins: the PotteryForm z-value drops by 1.87 SD units (from +0.74 to −1.13, the series minimum) in exactly the same interval in which the PotteryDecoration z-value rises by 1.45 SD units (from −0.48 to +0.97). The new regime is first visible in the 1700 BCE bin and persists essentially unchanged for the rest of the record (PotteryForm stays at −1.13 through 500 BCE; PotteryDecoration stays at +0.97 and later steps up to +1.53 at 1000 BCE, while PotteryForm remains collapsed). This transition falls at the descriptive boundary between the Late Neolithic (LN) and Older Bronze Age (OBA) period labels in the source table; no causal interpretation (e.g., via the pollen/openness series) is implied by the data."
